engine/barrier_coordination.py:R5:Barrie: Flagged pattern: `if isinstance(transform, GateSettings):` raising OrchestrationInvariantError. This is nominal NEGATIVE dispatch over a closed, ELSPETH-owned container, not a Tier-3 shape guard on external data. `transform` is the local return of `self._nav.resolve_plugin_for_node(node_id)`, whose signature is exactly `TransformProtocol | GateSettings | None` (engine/dag_navigator.py:157) and which raises OrchestrationInvariantError itself for any node that is neither plugin-bearing nor structural. The union therefore has three inhabitants and the method rejects the two known non-transform ones by name — `None` (structural coalesce/row-union node) on the preceding branch, `GateSettings` here — before asking the surviving value the only question that matters, `transform.is_batch_aware`. The isinstance is against a concrete class ELSPETH defines, which is precisely what ADR-032 prescribes for data ELSPETH owns. Critically, TransformProtocol conformance is deliberately NOT measured (ruling elspeth-8783933d99): a positive `isinstance(transform, TransformProtocol)` would be a runtime_checkable structural check, so a protocol-membership miss would masquerade as 'DAG/config inconsistency' and blame the graph for what is actually a plugin-contract defect. Naming GateSettings by its own defect keeps the three error messages attributable to three distinct causes. Not decorator-eligible: `transform` roots at a method call on `self._nav`, not at any parameter of `_adopt_aggregation_row`, so no `source_param` could ever cover it. WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS: `resolve_plugin_for_node` gaining a fourth return shape (the two negative arms would no longer exhaust the non-transform inhabitants and an unhandled shape would reach `.is_batch_aware` and fail with a misattributed AttributeError); GateSettings ceasing to be a distinct owned class; or a decision to reverse elspeth-8783933d99 and dispatch positively on TransformProtocol, which would reintroduce the structural-typing masquerade this arm exists to avoid.
engine/tokens.py:R5:TokenManager:create_: Flagged pattern: `if isinstance(source_row.row, dict):` selecting between `dict(source_row.row)` normalisation and `{"_raw": source_row.row}` envelope wrapping. This is a Tier-1 admission guard on ELSPETH's own audit-write path, not a Tier-3 parse. `SourceRow.row` is declared `Any` BY DESIGN (contracts/results.py, with the comment 'row is Any (not dict) because quarantined rows from external data may not be dicts (e.g., JSON arrays containing primitives like numbers)') — quarantine is exactly the arm that carries payloads which failed source validation, so a non-dict here is expected input, not an anomaly. The isinstance exists because the very next consumer is stricter than the field: `PipelineRow.__init__` (contracts/schema_contract.py:497) raises TypeError unless `type(data) is not dict` is false, i.e. it demands the exact builtin dict and refuses to coerce, precisely so a silently coerced list-of-tuples cannot mask corruption on a Tier-1 restore path. This branch is what makes both shapes representable in the audit trail without weakening that guard: a dict subclass (OrderedDict and friends) is flattened to a plain dict, a genuine non-mapping is preserved verbatim under `_raw` rather than being coerced or dropped. Nothing is silenced — the quarantined payload survives into `pipeline_row.to_dict()` and the epoch-fenced `create_quarantine_row_with_token` write (ADR-030 §C.4 row 9) either way. Deliberately NOT decorated: `@trust_boundary`/`@observation_boundary` is licensed only where the function 'actually parses external data', and `create_quarantine_token` parses nothing — it orchestrates a durable rows+token transaction, and this normalisation is one incidental step on the way there. Every live decorator in the tree sits on a genuine parse entry point (preflight.py, runtime_factory.py, llm/config_validation.py, llm/provider.py, aws_s3_sink.py, token_usage.from_dict); none is an engine method whose body is a DB write. A decorator would also suppress R1/R5 function-wide on every `source_row`-derived name, silently covering future `.get()` calls anywhere in this body, where the per-site entry covers exactly this one branch and falls due for judge renewal. WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS: narrowing `SourceRow.row` to `dict[str, Any]` (the non-dict arm becomes dead and the guard should go); PipelineRow relaxing its exact-dict admission (the subclass-normalisation arm becomes unnecessary); or the `_raw` envelope acquiring semantics beyond opaque preservation — e.g. any consumer indexing into it — which would make this a real parse and demand a Tier-3 boundary with a malformed-input test rather than a justification.
engine/batch_adapter.py:R5:SharedBatchAd: Flagged pattern: `if isinstance(entry.result, ExceptionResult): raise entry.result.exception`. Nominal narrowing of an ELSPETH-owned two-member union to reach a crash path, not a defensive shape check. `entry` is the `_WaiterEntry` returned by `self._pop_waiter_result(key)`, and its `result` field is declared `TransformResult | ExceptionResult | None` (engine/batch_adapter.py:69). ExceptionResult is a frozen ELSPETH dataclass (contracts/results.py:171) whose sole purpose is to ferry an uncaught worker-thread exception across the thread boundary so it can be re-raised in the orchestrator thread — the module docstring's 'Exception Propagation' contract, and the mechanism by which plugin bugs crash the pipeline instead of being swallowed by the async pattern. The isinstance is therefore the discriminator that decides crash-versus-return, and it is against a concrete owned class, exactly ADR-032's nominal arm. It cannot be replaced by a truthiness or attribute test without reintroducing the swallow it exists to prevent. The remaining `None` inhabitant is handled immediately below by an explicit OrchestrationInvariantError rather than being folded into this branch, so 'worker raised' and 'emit() signalled without setting a result' stay distinguishable defects. Not decorator-eligible: `entry` roots at an internal dict pop under `self._lock`, not at any parameter of `_wait_for`, and worker results are ELSPETH-produced, not external data. WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS: a new member joining the `_WaiterEntry.result` union (this arm would no longer partition it and the new shape would fall through to the None check and be misreported as an emit()-ordering violation); ExceptionResult gaining subclasses that must be dispatched differently; or the worker pool moving to a mechanism that propagates exceptions natively across threads, which would delete the wrapper and this branch with it.
core/landscape/formatters.py:R5:CSVForma: Flagged pattern: `if isinstance(value, Mapping):` — the recurse-and-flatten arm of the CSV dot-notation walker. This is closed-set structural dispatch over the JSON type lattice of already-integrity-verified data, not a trust boundary. The production caller is `_parse_verified_records` (plugins/sinks/_audit_export_bundle_effects.py:412), which reads newline-framed chunks through `reader.iter_verified_chunks()` and rejects any frame that is not a byte-exact canonical JSON object (`canonical_json(value).encode('utf-8') != frame`) BEFORE `formatter.format(record)` is reached. What arrives is therefore ELSPETH-authored audit data whose bytes have already been hash-verified — Tier-1 material, not an external parse — and whose value shapes are exactly what `json.loads` can yield. `Mapping` rather than `dict` is the right test because `flatten` is also its own caller: line 51 recurses with `dict(value.items())`, and the class must accept any mapping an in-process caller hands it. This arm is load-bearing for audit fidelity in a way the `else` arm is not: it carries the empty-mapping rule, writing the literal string "{}" so that an auditor can distinguish 'config was explicitly empty' from 'config was not present' — a distinction that would be destroyed if empty mappings recursed into zero columns. Both exits guard `full_key in result` and raise ValueError on collision rather than overwriting, so no flattening path can silently lose a column. Not decorator-eligible: `value` does root at the `record` parameter, but the data is not external, so `tier=3` would be a false claim about provenance and the decorator would misdescribe a verified-audit walker as an untrusted-input boundary. WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS: `_parse_verified_records` (or a new caller) invoking `format()` before the canonical-JSON verification, which would make this genuinely Tier-3 and demand a boundary rather than a justification; the flattener being pointed at non-JSON inputs such as dataclasses or sets, where `Mapping`/`list` no longer partition the value space; or the empty-mapping-as-"{}" convention being retired, which removes this arm's audit-semantics justification and reduces it to plain recursion.

Flagged pattern: `elif isinstance(value, list):` — the JSON-string-encoding arm, a DIFFERENT mechanism from the Mapping arm above it, which recurses. A list cannot be flattened into dot-notation columns because CSV has no nested representation and the arity is data-dependent (two rows of the same record type would disagree on column count), so the only lossless option is to serialise the whole list into one cell: `json.dumps(serialize_datetime(value))`. The inner `serialize_datetime` call is not cosmetic — it is the audit-integrity gate, raising AuditIntegrityError on NaN and Infinity (core/landscape/serialization.py) and normalising datetimes to ISO strings, so a non-canonical float inside a nested list is rejected at export rather than being written into a CSV cell as the token `NaN`. `list` and not `Sequence` is the correct test here precisely because the input is `json.loads` output: JSON arrays decode to builtin lists and nothing else, and widening to Sequence would capture `str`, which must fall through to the scalar `else` arm or every string cell would be re-encoded with quotes. Tuples likewise stay out of this arm; they are unreachable on the verified path for the same reason (`json.loads` never yields one) and the scalar arm's `serialize_datetime` would convert one to a list anyway. Like its sibling, this branch guards `full_key in result` and raises ValueError rather than overwriting. Not decorator-eligible for the same provenance reason as the Mapping arm: the bytes are hash-verified ELSPETH audit data, so `tier=3` would be untrue. WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THIS: tuples or other non-list sequences becoming reachable — which happens the moment a caller feeds `flatten` anything other than verified `json.loads` output — since they would then silently take the scalar arm and be written un-encoded; `serialize_datetime` losing its NaN/Infinity rejection, which is the only thing making this arm safe to JSON-encode; or CSV export gaining a real nested representation, which would turn this into a recursion arm like its sibling.
